try_objects_and_event_records_sketch0.prompt: Now apply what you just learned in this task. Problem: A library system needs the title, author, and page count to travel together as one book record instead of as unrelated variables. Task: Create `book` with `title`, `author`, and `pages` properties, then log the title and page count. Expected result: the Console shows values read from the same object. Produce the result for create a book record so it reinforces Objects and Event Records.

help.concept: An object groups related values under named properties.
help.hint_1: Use an object literal assigned to `book`.
help.hint_2: Read `book.title` and `book.pages` when you log the result.

try_objects_and_event_records_sketch1.title: Try it yourself: Update a game character
try_objects_and_event_records_sketch1.prompt: Now apply what you just learned in this task. Problem: A game character's health belongs to that character record and must change when the character takes damage. Task: Create `player` with `name` and `health`. Reduce `player.health` by 20, then log the updated health. Expected result: the Console shows the reduced health value from the player object. Produce the result for update a game character so it reinforces Objects and Event Records.
try_objects_and_event_records_sketch1.hint: Keep the same object and change only one property.

help.concept: A property inside a const object can still be updated.
help.hint_1: Start health at a numeric value large enough to subtract 20.
help.hint_2: Assign `player.health - 20` back to `player.health` before logging it.

try_objects_and_event_records_sketch2.prompt: Now apply what you just learned in this task. Problem: A product catalog contains multiple products with the same data shape, and the storefront needs to read one product from the collection. Task: Create `products` as an array of two objects with `name` and `price` properties. Log the name of the second product. Expected result: the Console shows the second product's name. Produce the result for read from a product catalog so it reinforces Objects and Event Records.
try_objects_and_event_records_sketch2.hint: Read the array item first, then its property.

help.concept: Arrays can hold structured objects, and indexing can select one record before dot notation reads a property.
help.hint_1: The collection should contain two object literals.
help.hint_2: Use the second array position, then `.name`.

objects-facts-multi.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
objects-facts-multi.hint: Distinguish object properties from array positions.

help.concept: Objects use named properties; const keeps the binding stable but does not freeze every property.

arrays-of-objects.title: Arrays and objects work together
arrays-of-objects.bodyMarkdown:
Real programs often need many structured records. Put objects inside an array when you need a collection of things that share the same kinds of properties.

```js
const events = [
  { name: "Jazz Night", room: "Music Center" },
  { name: "Robotics Lab", room: "Engineering Hall" }
];

console.log(events[1].name);
```

Line by line:

1. `events` is an array with two items.
2. Each item is an object with `name` and `room` properties.
3. `events[1]` reads the second object.
4. `.name` then reads the `name` property from that object.

This combination—**array of objects**—becomes the main data shape for the rest of the course.
